findings.summary: Two of the five contour levels are not separable at the size the figure is read, so the level of a contour cannot be read off the map. render.py:61 declares the styles as (solid, (0,(6,2)), (0,(2,2)), dotted, dashdot) for the levels 0.04, 0.05, 0.06, 0.08, 0.12 percent, all in one blue. Measured on the rendered PNG at 1399x720 the 0.05% handle is a 21 px dash, 8 px gap, 1 px mark and the 0.12% handle is a 23 px dash, 6 px gap, 2 px mark: a 2 px difference in dash length and gap, and both read as 'long dash plus tick'. Downscaled to the 900 px page column the two handles render identically. The wall-targets panel reaches 0.146%, so 0.12% contours exist and mark the largest differences the figure was produced to show; a reader cannot tell them from the 0.05% set. The median and maximum printed under each panel survive, but the per-contour spatial reading the line-contour map exists for does not. The repair is style-only: five dash styles that separate at page width, or lightness steps of the one hue, with the data and the level array unchanged.

notes: Read only: no file was edited, created, moved or redrawn; the record is the only artifact written.

Every quantitative label in all five figures was reconciled against the run's receipts and matches to the printed digits: frame residuals and converged flags and lower X-point offsets against gpu/comparison.json and recovery-179-head/comparison.json, and the three median/maximum pairs against gpu/base/frame-137-diverted/coupling-differences.json.
The four flux panels use one legend across both panels and one colour per quantity, so the solved, EFIT and wall semantics are consistent figure to figure and across the four frames.

The EFIT axis marker is drawn larger than the solved one and protrudes where the two coincide, so the page caption's claim that the dark reference markers remain visible beneath the blue ones is true in the rendered image.
